01 — Foundation

Brand Overview

LLIS is a place where young people discover who they are, find their voice, and build the connections that shape their future. Every brand decision flows from three core values: Caring, Creation, Connection.

Mission Statement

Lënster Lycée International School nurtures every student's potential through an education that is rigorous, compassionate, and globally minded — grounded in the nature, heritage, and multilingual richness of Luxembourg.

Vision

To be the leading secondary school in the Grand Duchy where academic excellence and personal development are inseparable — producing graduates who are critical thinkers, empathetic citizens, and creative contributors to the world.

Core Values — The Three Cs

🤝

Caring

We put people first. Every communication leads with empathy. Teachers know students by name and by story.

✨

Creation

Learning is an act of making. We reward curiosity and design spaces that invite creative risk-taking.

🌐

Connection

We connect students to ideas, to each other, and to the wider world. Our identity system itself is built on interconnecting forms.

02 — Logo

Logo Guidelines

The LLIS mark is a rounded rectangle containing two interlocked diagonal strokes — an abstraction of L and I, evoking infinity, technology, and the dynamic exchange between students and ideas.

Official Logo Variants

Always use the original vector PDF files for production. These previews are for reference.

Solid vs. Outline — When to Use Which

The LLIS logo exists in two structural variants. Choosing the right one for the right context ensures optimal legibility and brand consistency across all media.

LLIS Solid

The primary variant. The filled form of the mark gives maximum visual weight and impact. Use Solid as the default for all standard applications.

  • Letterheads, official documents, business cards
  • Website header and digital communications
  • Large-format print where detail is visible
  • Embroidery and merchandise (≥ 40 mm)

LLIS Outline

The secondary variant. The line-based form gives elegance and refinement for contexts where Solid would be too heavy or where the printing technique requires restraint.

  • Engraving, embossing, laser cutting
  • Watermarks and background treatments
  • Fine print applications (stationery, gift items)
  • Situations where ink coverage must be minimal

Clear Space & Minimum Size

📐

Clear Space Rule

Maintain clear space equal to the height of the capital "L" in the wordmark on all four sides. In practice this is approximately equal to the full height of the logo mark itself.

ContextMin HeightFormat
Digital / Web / App40 pxSVG — never upscale raster
Print — documents15 mmPDF vector
Large format / signage60 mmEPS — never JPG
Favicon / App iconMark only (32 px)ICO / PNG

Do & Don't

✅ Do

  • Use approved colour versions only
  • Maintain defined clear space at all times
  • Use the mark alone when space is very limited
  • Use vector files for all print output
  • Ensure minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1

❌ Don't

  • Stretch, skew, or distort proportions
  • Rotate the logo mark
  • Apply drop shadows or glow effects
  • Place on busy backgrounds without a container
  • Recolour individual mark elements
  • Substitute unofficial typefaces in the wordmark

04 — Typography

Typography

LLIS uses Gill Sans as its primary typeface — a humanist sans-serif with rounded geometry that balances academic authority with approachability. A persistent problem with standard Gill Sans requires a deliberate solution.

⚠️

The 1 / I Problem — and How We Solve It

In standard Gill Sans, uppercase I (eye) and numeral 1 (one) are visually identical — plain vertical strokes with no distinguishing features. This causes real errors in student IDs, class codes (11IS, 1IB), room numbers, and timetables.

Gill Sans — ambiguous

1IIS · 11IB
Problem

Source Code Pro — clear

1IIS · 11IB
Solution

Solution 1 — Gill Sans Nova

Upgrade to Gill Sans Nova (Monotype, included in Microsoft 365). The Nova version redesigns numeral shapes and adds OpenType features. Use for all official documents.

Solution 2 — Source Code Pro for Codes

For all alphanumeric codes — student IDs, class codes, room numbers — switch to Source Code Pro. Free on Google Fonts; designed so 0/O/1/I/l are all distinct.

Solution 3 — Nunito for Digital

In Canva and web where Gill Sans is unavailable, use Nunito (Google Fonts, free). It shares Gill Sans' rounded humanist quality with clearly distinct 1 and I.

05 — Imagery

Imagery & Photography

LLIS photography tells the story of real people doing real things — learning, creating, connecting. It should feel documentary and warm, never staged or stock-photo generic.

☀️

Natural Light First

Prioritise warm-toned daylight. Luxembourg's golden morning light through classroom windows is a signature look. Avoid cold, fluorescent lighting.

🎯

Human-Centred

Students are subjects, not props. Capture genuine moments of collaboration, concentration, discovery and joy. Shallow depth-of-field draws focus.

🌿

Rooted in Place

Frame subjects with Luxembourg's nature — forests, open skies, the Müllerthal landscape. Even indoor shots benefit from greenery in frame.

🌍

Authentically Diverse

Photography must authentically reflect LLIS's multinational community across nationalities, abilities, and learning styles. No tokenism.

Style Tones

✅ Nature & campus — use freely
✅ Learning moments — preferred
✅ Celebration & community
❌ Cold / desaturated / gloomy
❌ Generic stock imagery
✅ Achievement & awards moments

Image Treatment on Backgrounds

  • Apply Sage or Midnight colour overlay (20–30% opacity) when placing text over images
  • Never use heavy vignettes or black overlays — the brand is warm, not dramatic
  • Duotone in Midnight + Sage is acceptable for campaign graphics
  • Never apply heavy Instagram-style filters, oversaturation, or artificial HDR effects
06 — Voice

Voice & Tone

LLIS communicates the way a caring, knowledgeable mentor would — clear, encouraging, precise, and never condescending. We speak to students as capable people, to parents as trusted partners.

Clear, not clever

Plain language. No jargon or marketing fluff. Every sentence serves a purpose.

Warm, not informal

Approachable and human, but professionally respectful. Never "Hey guys!" in official communication.

Encouraging, not empty

Praise must be specific. "Your project shows strong analytical thinking" is LLIS. "Amazing work!" is not.

Multilingual aware

Tone adapts per language — formal French, approachable English, precise German, warm Luxembourgish.

Tone by Context

ContextToneExample
AdmissionsWarm, confident, welcoming"We'd love to show you around — every LLIS student has a home here."
AcademicPrecise, encouraging, professional"Your results show real progress in critical analysis. Here's how to build on that."
Student-facing digitalDirect, positive (never condescending)"Your IB deadline is Friday 14 June. Need help? Book a session with your supervisor."
Crisis / urgentClear, calm, factual — no drama"We have received notification of [situation]. Here is what is happening and what to do."
CelebrationGenuinely proud, specific, joyful"Our class of 2026 achieved a 98% IB pass rate — the strongest in LLIS history."
Social mediaLively, authentic, brief"Science Week is here 🔬 Day 1: students built aquatic ecosystems from scratch."

Word Choices

✅ Use these

  • nurture · grow · develop
  • community · together · belong
  • curious · explore · discover
  • rigour · challenge · excellence
  • rooted · grounded · place
  • multilingual · international
  • caring · empathy · wellbeing
  • create · make · build
  • nature · landscape · environment
  • connect · bridge · link

❌ Avoid these

  • "world-class" — vague, overused
  • "cutting-edge" — cliché
  • "leverage" — corporate jargon
  • "synergy" — meaningless
  • "paradigm shift" — academic jargon
  • "stakeholders" for parents/students
  • "best-in-class" — untestable
  • "dynamic learners" — buzzword
  • Exclamation marks in official docs
  • Passive voice where avoidable

Before / After

✅ LLIS Voice

  • "Applications for 2026–27 open on 1 September."
  • "We're proud of every student who crossed the stage today."
  • "The library is open until 18:00 weekdays. Drop in, read, think."

❌ Not LLIS

  • "Exciting news — applications are OPEN! 🎉🎉"
  • "LLIS is proud to leverage world-class educational synergies."
  • "Please be advised that the library facility will remain accessible during extended hours."

WCAG 2.1 AA — Minimum Standard

All text: 4.5:1 contrast minimum. Interactive elements need visible focus states. Touch targets minimum 44×44 px. All images carry descriptive alt text. Forms always use associated label elements — never placeholder-only.

Canva Brand Kit

1 — Brand Colors

Brand Kit → Colors. Add each hex: Midnight, Steel, Sage, Fern, Terracotta, Blush, Amber, Charcoal, Slate, Cream. Name them exactly as shown.

2 — Brand Fonts

Set Heading + Body to Gill Sans (or Nunito). Set a third slot to Source Code Pro for codes/IDs.

3 — Upload Logos

Brand Kit → Logos. Upload all four variants: Solid, Outline, White knockout, Mark-only. Use the provided PDFs.

Warm, academic, nature-connected. Secondary school in Luxembourg.
